findings.title: Seven AI routes have no rate limit
findings.body: These mounts call Claude or Gemini but are registered in server/index.js without aiLimiter, and the route files do not add it themselves. A runaway client loop or a shared login could run up model spend. Add aiLimiter at the mount, as the guide-chat routes already do.

evidence.text: app.use('/api/tasks', require('./routes/tasks'))  // tasks.js uses callModel + messages.stream
app.use('/api/mood', requireFeature('mood'), ...)  // mood.js streams from Anthropic
/api/gmail (public mount, check which handlers call a model)

findings.title: Hardcoded model fallbacks remain
findings.body: Your rule is that model ids come from Settings through getModelsForUser. Property Scenario falls back to a fixed claude-sonnet-4-6 when no setting resolves, and chat.js keeps a FALLBACK_MODELS list (Claude 4.6, Gemini 2.0/2.5 preview) that will go stale. The TTS default in voiceProviders.js is env-overridable and lower risk.

evidence.text: const FALLBACK_MODELS = [ claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6, gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06 ]

findings.title: A cron job reaches into a route file for Finance logic
findings.body: server/cron/recurringCron.js requires routes/finance.js in four places to post journals, and finance.js requires the cron back, making an import cycle. Business logic living in a 4,700-line route file is why. Move posting and date helpers into a services/finance module that both can import.

findings.title: Big files that keep changing
findings.body: Files that are both very large and edited often are where bugs and merge pain concentrate. db.js changed in 103 of the last 600 commits; every tool adds its tables there. Splitting it into per-tool schema modules (called in order from db.js) and breaking the largest pages into sub-components would make each change smaller.

findings.title: Eleven tools have no tests; Wellbeing has one for 14,500 lines
findings.body: Most tools are well covered (404 test files overall). The gaps are concentrated: Product Scout (7.8k lines), Recipes (4.8k), SEO (3.8k), Contract Review (3.5k), Google Ads, News Digest, Mood, Search Console, Browser Agent, Suggestions, and Student. Wellbeing has 14.5k lines with a single test. Start with the ones that call paid APIs or handle money.

findings.title: 23 tools have no guide chat
findings.body: CLAUDE.md says every new tool follows the Video Tools conventions, including a guide chat. 36 tools have one; the gaps are mostly older tools (Tasks, Chat, CRM sub-pages, Mood, Goals, Recipes, the SEO family, Property, Wellbeing). Adding one is cheap with guideCore and the shared TutorChat.

findings.title: Restyle and Web Extractor services are tangled
findings.body: Six files across two tools import each other in a loop (restyle/loadFromUrl, scrapeCss, inlineImages, selfContainedPage, webExtractorService, webExtractorPalette). Changing one tool can break the other. Pull the shared page-fetch and CSS-scrape code into one module both depend on.

findings.title: Raw fetch and direct icon imports in a few places
findings.body: Two spots bypass apiClient (file upload/preview in Chat, backup create/restore in Admin), likely for FormData or blobs. If apiClient lacks a FormData path, add one so auth and error handling stay in one place. ArtifactPanel and UrlBar import lucide-react directly instead of getIcon.

findings.title: 31 tools delete without the recycle bin
findings.body: Delete routes exist but moveToBin is not used in their code. Many are fine (cached lookups, logs), but some hold user content: Finance, CRM, Recipes, Wellbeing, Fitness, Property, Contract Review, Redaction. Decide per tool and record the decision in its doc.

findings.title: Leftover backups and possibly unused files
findings.body: server/db_bk.js and server/index_bk.js are old copies. Five small files have no importers and no string references; verify, then delete.
